tastingNotes:
Good acidity gives vibrant freshness, acidity
and textures from limited skin contact
balanced by mid-full body. There is a refined
roundness, which comes from the style of
winemaking. Mid-palate intensity comes
from the unique trellising system used by Apogee.
The richer style is somewhere between
Alsace Gris and Italian Grigio.

100% French oak. A bright ruby, elegant and poised red wine, with a slippery and full
mouthfeel, mild tannins and roundness. Perfumes are red berry summer pudding and beautifully integrated
oak. The palate finishes with blueberry and raspberry and mild, toasty oak. For current drinking, but the tannin/acid
framework will permit extended aging for 10 years.
pairings: roast chicken, duck breast with cherries, Brillat-Savarin soft-ripened cheese.
authorNotes:
Humid climates can give the perfect mix of berry perfumes and forest floor characters. These shape this
wine, and it take it closer to Burgundy in style than many New World versions.

tastingNotes: The nose opens with vibrant red fruits of strawberry, raspberry, and cherry bursting from the glass. Beneath this exuberance lies a deeper layer of fig, olive and subtle savoury notes, signaling the richness and longevity that will unfold with age.
awards: Awarded 95 points by James Halliday and a Gold Medal at the Australian Pinot Noir Challenge
authorNotes: will continue to evolve beautifully over the next 8–10 years, gaining even more depth, harmony, and delicious complexity.

tastingNotes: With brilliant acidity and a refined structure, the 2023 Bangor Chardonnay offers hallmark citrus, white peach, and subtle summer meadow notes, complemented by vanilla, cashew and lemon butter richness, before a long, mouth-watering finish.
pairings: seafood, chicken, cheese plates and creamy pasta dishes.
authorNotes: Enjoy now or cellar 5 to 10 years.

tastingNotes: Bellebonne Bis is about absolute floral and fruit gorgeousness. The aromas are a melody of strawberry, Turkish delight and rose petal. The palate is elegant and long with textures of fresh cream, brioche and delicate fruit.
authorNotes: ‘Bis’ is French for ‘the space in-between’, which encapsulates the process and inspiration it took to make this exquisite non-vintage rosé.

tastingNotes: Made from 100% Tasmanian Pinot Noir, this is delicate pink with salmon blush and super fine bubbles. The aromas are a meld of strawberry, marzipan, Turkish delight and buttery pastry. While the flavours are subtle, there is a delicious roundness in the mouth set against a fine tannin finish with the barest touch of bitter orange pith.

This wine shows lifted aromas of lime blossom, green apple, nashi pear and wet stone. The palate is crisp and vibrant, mirroring the nose with a saline streak and a hint of kaffir lime leaf that lifts the fruit. Bright acidity keeps the wine precise and focused; the texture is sleek with a chalky, citrus-driven finish of excellent length.
pairings: Grilled Tasmanian Flathead, lemon dressed oysters, spicy asian salads, Goat's cheese tartlettes
awards: 94 points / Premium rating, 2025 Canberra International Riesling Challenge

tastingNotes: A delightfully fresh bouquet of flowers, red fruits (cherries, plums, raspberries), cedar and spice. The palate is similarly fresh and lithe, showcasing similar flavours, subtle and integrated tannins and a long finish carrying red fruits, a hint of cocoa and spice.
pairings: With excellent fine tannins and a long finish, this wine would suit a wide range of foods, such as Raddoch farm quail with a pomegranate salad.
awards: The Angelo Puglisi Trophy Grand Champion, 2025 Royal Queensland Wine Awards

tastingNotes: Vibrant aromas of red plum and raspberry, lifted by subtle notes of spice and dried herbs. The palate is smooth and generous, with a delicious core of bright fruit framed by silky, finely textured tannins. Balanced acidity brings freshness and length, finishing with poise and quiet savoury complexity.

A flavoursome, dry rose with a good balance of fruit and texture. Fresh red berries, cherries, wild strawberries and a little spice. 100% Pinot Noir, whole bunch pressed then cool fermented to dryness. Full malolactic fermentation.

This chardonnay was meticulously hand-harvested with ripeness and purity in mind. Whole bunch pressed and cold settled overnight, fruit is then gently transferred to French oak for ferment and maturation. A fine expression of cool-climate Chardonnay – floral, citrus and stone fruit aromatics blend seamlessly with toasted oak characteristics.

The fruit was hand-picked and gently pressed, allowing the delicate flavours to shine through. Bunches of white flowers, particularly jasmine, lift the bouquet with nots of apricot, star fruit, and lemon zest beneath.

The palate is lively with zippy acidity and layers of texture.

Aromatics mellowing from   flash, brash youth into a perfumed nose with hints of lemon/lime, granny smith apple & honeysuckle. This Chablis style wine offers a satisfying mouth feel on the palate & texture with the most mouthwatering, long- lasting Nashi pear and honeydew melon balancing the soft & clean citrusy finish to perfection.

Bright ruby red colour, spicy aroma, toffee and vanilla. On the palate delicate fruit driven style, mixed berries overlaying some cherry, blackcurrant, caramel, vanilla and a finely balanced layer of tannin. The oak and fruit combining well together to give this wine depth, length and finish.

made from 85% of our Pinot Noir and 15% of our Chardonnay grapes. 
 
Our Rosé gives delicious bursts of fresh apple blossom with hints of cherry, raspberry fruits and lemon zest. It's light and refreshing
It shows notes of citrus and red apple with toasted biscuit aroma and fine creamy texture

A vibrant, deep ruby red with lifted aromas of blackcurrant and dark cherry.  Enticing secondary aromas of tobacco leaf, black olive and subtle vanillin.  An elegant style of Cabernet Sauvignon with the palate displaying mixed berry fruits of dark cherry and blueberry, a line of redcurrant acidity giving continuity.  Abundant fine-grained tannins will ensure the longevity of this wine and reward those who wish to hide it in their cellar for many years.

Deep ruby red in colour, this wine has powerful aromas of dark cherry, raspberry, subtle spice and toasty oak.  Concentrated red fruits fill the palate with ripe, fine-grained tannins providing structure and length.
Aged in French oak. Flavours of black currant, cigar leaf, plum, black cherry and green pepper
risp yet elegant palate with a classic combination of typical buttery notes, citrus and tropical fruit.
pairings: The ideal food pairings are oysters, creamy soft cheeses and white meat. Further great matches are sashimi, grilled fish and mussels or mushrooms and spicy dishes

tastingNotes: Pale straw with green hues, this wine reveals a bouquet of citrus, white peach, and green apple. The palate is layered with subtle hints of sea spray and toasted bread, adding complexity and charm.
awards: Top Gold, Grapeworks Trophy & #2 of 170 NV Sparkling Wines in Australia - Tasmanian Wine Show 2025

tastingNotes: Showcasing the best of the unheralded Pinot Meunier, this Meunier et Noir multi-vintage has a pale straw colour and a fine, persistent mousse. Aromas of strawberry, raspberry, and rose-water carry through to the palate. The richness from the two red varieties is beautifully balanced by a small amount of Chardonnay, giving the wine a long, lingering finish.

has aromas of toasty brioche and a luscious mousse of silky soft bubbles. It follows through with a hint of strawberry and apple that dance on the palate. It is made in the traditional method and has spent 18 months on lees.

A dry and refreshing Riesling which is pale straw in colour. This aromatic wine has subtle citrus blossom and musk on the nose and leads into a bright, juicy and crisp palate. Great natural acidity makes this a beautiful match with a broad range of foods

exceptionally easy-drinking. Matured in stainless steel tanks, this pinot gris features notes of banana, pear, apples and a hint of spice giving this wine a vibrant and memorable experience and finishes slightly dry

It is a beautiful dark crimson colour. With aromas of red and black forest fruits and subtle notes of vanilla and spice.  The palate shows juicy red and black fruits with a fine tannin structure and moorish acidity that renders this wine immediately approachable.
authorNotes: Comes from the oldest vines on the Freycinet coast. Will cellar for 8-10 years.  Hand plunged twice daily for nine days. Wine was then transferred to French oak barriques, matured in barrel for 12 months prior to blending and finishing for bottling.

tastingNotes: Riesling’s varietal characters shine through with floral aromas and notes of lime, quince, apricot and tropical fruit. The palate is impeccably balanced, featuring citrus peel, quince and cumquat flavours and a lightly honeyed note with zesty acidity driving through to a long and refreshing finish.
pairings: Ideal with fruit based desserts such as baked quince, and softer blue cheeses.

tastingNotes: the bouquet features the classic pinot characters of spice and black cherry — French oak tannins enhance the firm full-flavoured palate.

Bright ruby in colour with moderate intensity, typical of the variety. Aromas of cut plum, blackcurrant and boysenberry with hints of blue florals such as violets, subtle spice and savoury notes that will develop. The medium bodied palate has crisp, crunchy, texture and bright acidity with vibrant red and blue fruits.
pairings: Ideal for spring and summer with grilled salmon, terrines, mushroom risotto or slightly chilled as an aperitif.
authorNotes: The fruit was partially hand-picked, 3% of whole bunches and the destemmed balance were placed in an open top fermenter. Fermentation commenced naturally after three days and concluded five days later with gentle twice daily plunging. The wine was then drained into a tank with pressings added back for one day before being racked to one year and older French oak barriques. The wine underwent malolactic fermentation during its 5 months in barrel.

tastingNotes: Initial aromas of fresh cranberries, toasted spice and ripe tamarillo. These aromas are enhanced with earthy notes and dark plum after some time in the glass. The palate has attractive dark fruit with classic Tasmanian acidity, this is accompanied by complex herbal notes and a lingering finish with a touch of oak spice.
pairings:
Baked gnocchi with wild mushrooms and pesto parmesan bechamel. Roast pork with pistachio stuffing served with braised leeks and creamy butternut mash.
Treatment
authorNotes: Fermentation started after two to three days and continued for four to five days, with five to twenty percent whole bunches, depending on site. The cap was plunged up to three times a day to extract colour and tannin from the skins. The wine was then pressed and settled before being placed into French oak barriques (20% new) for 9 months, where malolactic fermentation took place prior to filtration and bottling.

tastingNotes: A full bodied East Coast Pinot Noir with flavours of cherries, berries and just a hint of spice
an elegant wine with flavours of stone fruit and just a touch of oak.
authorNotes: This wine will cellar well for 5 years or more.

tastingNotes: A blend of chardonnay and pinot noir, it is a fresh and lifted fruit-driven aroma of apples, white blossoms and lemongrass. The palate is zesty and bright, with hints of complex hazelnut and brioche bread. The texture of this wine is firm but elegant with lemony acidity giving length to the delicately creamy palate.
pairings: A classic match with natural oysters, lobster and white-fleshed fish.
authorNotes: Handpicked, whole bunch pressed with 100% MLF, the NV Cuvée is made using the traditional method of bottle fermentation. Blending, a key aspect of this wine, is always focused on retaining the distinctive fruit characteristics whilst balancing the more complex flavours that come with wine maturation in barrel and on yeast lees. The varietal blend is 69% Chardonnay and 31% Pinot Noir, with 20% reserve wine blended into the 2023 base. The reserve blend consists of 2% 2022, 7% 2021, 4% 2020, 9% 2005-2019 (perpetual reserve). Tirage Date: September 2023, Disgorgement Date: 14/05/2025 (20 months tirage-age).

tastingNotes: Mature Sparkling Rosé character; a pale salmon colour and a fresh strawberry and musk aroma, complexed by hints of lanolin and toast. But there is an added layer of complexity from the bottle-aged reserve in this delicious 2023 blend.
pairings: A perfect match for freshly shaved prosciutto, figs and Parmesan. Soft white cheeses, oysters, hot smoked salmon or a roast capsicum salad would all be fine accompaniments.
authorNotes:
This benchmark Tasmanian sparkling wine continues to be crafted from 100% pinot noir grapes. The 20% reserve consists of 8% 2021, 8% 2020,
3% 2019 and 1% 2018. All reserve wine is aged in old hogshead (300l) barrels.
100% Malo-lactic.
Tirage Date: September 2023, Disgorgement Date: 23/05/2025 (20 months tirage-age)

tastingNotes: on the nose: mandarin, lime, honeysuckle. on the palate: Citrus, sherbet, chalky phenolics, bright acid finish.

Some key features to look for are a focused fruit profile, the unique acid line, wild yeast, ultra-fine solids, integrated oak, multiple strain malolactic impact, touches of autolysis. A style that evolves and grows with bottle age.
pairings: Raw fish, Lightly cooked shellfish - crab, prawns. Fish, Chicken, Pasta, Risotto.
awards:
James Halliday Australian Chardonnay and Cabernet Challenge
Top Gold
2023
authorNotes: The whole bunches go direct to the inert gas press. The juice flow from the press is ruthlessly cut with only the pristine juice from the middle of the press cycle going straight to New French oak. We allow natural yeast to carry out primary fermentation. During it’s time in oak no Sulphur is added. Lees stirred fortnightly for the11 months in oak. Malolactic fermentation happens in the spring on 100% of this wine. Filtered and bottled.
